title: First chapter of my browser RPG: a thief, a stolen purse and an old knight who won't fight. What do you think?
author: l1vi
selftext:
Hi all!

Looking for feedback on the opening of Evin's Echo, a story-first pixel RPG that plays in the browser. It's Book I of Tales of Solaria, a fantasy saga that started as voice notes I recorded on a trip to Ireland a few years back.

On the AI side: I don't have a coding background, so the whole game was built by directing AI rather than writing code myself. Claude handled the code from my scene scripts and design notes, and the painted cutscenes were made with ChatGPT image generation. The story, characters and lore are mine, and the hardest part was keeping the AI faithful to that canon from scene to scene. The game ships as a single self-contained HTML file, which made hosting on itch and my own site really simple.

The prologue starts around 0:14, Chapter One (pickpocketing in the market) around 0:40, and the Old Knight encounter around 0:55. Instead of just swinging at him you can Check, Talk, Apologize or Boast, and dodge his attacks in between.

I'd love to know whether mixing painted cutscenes with pixel gameplay works or feels jarring, whether the dialogue pacing is too slow for a first impression, and whether this clip makes you want to play the next chapter. And for anyone else making story-heavy games with AI, how are you keeping your characters consistent between scenes?

If you want to try it, it's free in the browser: https://talesofsolaria.itch.io/evins-tale

More Solaria games (and the Discord) on my site: https://talesofsolaria.co.uk/games/

Thanks for watching!
